title_original: ‘They pulled a guy’s face off. It’s my favourite bit!’ Linda Cardellini on Freaks and Geeks, Mad Men and slasher horror Crystal Lake
editorial_title_zh: “他们扯掉了一个人的脸。这是我最喜欢的片段！”琳达·卡德里尼谈《平常与怪异》、《广告狂人》与砍杀恐怖片《水晶湖》
editorial_excerpt_zh: 她在《广告狂人》中曾让唐·德雷珀（Don Draper）备受煎熬，并刚刚凭借《圣路易斯DTF》（DTF St Louis）赢得艾美奖。但当她转向恐怖片、参演《十三号星期五》（Friday the 13th）前传时，没有任何事能让她为随之而来的血腥场面做好心理准备。“第一次手里拿着那颗牙齿时，”琳达·卡德里尼（Linda Cardellini）说道，“我想：‘哦……’
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我第一次把那颗牙拿在手里时，”琳达·卡德里尼（Linda Cardellini）说道，“我想，‘哦天哪，这就是我正在做的事。’”因出演《怪胎与书呆子》（Freaks and Geeks）、《急诊室的故事》（ER）、《死丫头》（Dead to Me）、《广告狂人》（Mad Men）以及最近为其赢得艾美奖的《圣路易斯DTF》（DTF St Louis）而闻名的这位明星，正在谈论她向纯正恐怖片的转型。在《十三号星期五》（Friday the 13th）电影的前传《水晶湖》（Crystal Lake）中，卡德里尼饰演帕梅拉·沃希斯（Pamela Voorhees），即1980年原作中的最初杀人狂。顺便一提，那颗牙齿是人类的，嵌在帕姆的指关节里——直到她用一声毛骨悚然、令人作呕的咕叽声将其猛地拔出。", "links": [{"text": "Mad Men", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/mad-men-tv-series"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "普通的电影观众可能会把《黑色星期五13》和戴着曲棍球面具的连环杀手杰森联系在一起。但资深影迷会知道，杰森的母亲帕姆才是第一部电影里的反派。“他直到第三部电影才戴上面具，”卡德里尼说道，显然她做过功课。“帕姆才是最初的凶手，她是为了复仇而杀人。”（《水晶湖》对以往的故事线做了一些调整，比如把杰森溺水的时间从20世纪50年代改到了70年代初，但鉴于这个系列曾经灵活到让杰森去过太空，这种时间线上的微调倒也合情合理。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/77b9c82d286c77293e353d5b810f2188578d0b67/0_504_3857_3086/master/3857.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "琳达·卡德里尼微笑着，身穿白色连衣裙，双手叉腰摆出姿势", "caption": "“我喜欢不断变换风格”……琳达·卡德里尼。摄影：Valérie Macon/AFP/Getty Images", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《黑色星期五13》系列拥有忠实的观众群体——而《水晶湖》的运作人布拉德·卡勒布·凯恩就是其中之一。“他是如此狂热的粉丝，”卡德里尼说，“我觉得他会清楚粉丝们想要什么。”凯恩在看过她在Netflix惊悚剧《死寂》中的表演后，专门为她量身打造了这个角色，这让她感到很意外。“我最大的疑问是，‘我怎么会成为你脑海中首先浮现的合适人选呢？’”她笑着说。接拍《黑色星期五13》让他们感到压力了吗？“这让人望而生畏，但希望这也是一个机会，能让人看到某些原本没有获得独立发展空间的题材。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "任何在20世纪80年代和90年代成长起来的人（就像卡德里尼一样，她今年51岁）都会记得那些租来VHS录像带的留宿派对，每当弗莱迪·克鲁格、迈克尔·迈尔斯或杰森·沃希斯出现在银幕上时，总会伴随着阵阵尖叫。“那几乎是禁果，”她说，“本来不应该看，但你还是会看。不仅是血腥，还有性——所有那些你不该看的东西。我想，这正是年轻时的吸引力所在。它显得像是禁区，充满了叛逆色彩。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她喜欢惊吓桥段和血浆，这倒很合适，因为《水晶湖》里到处都是这些元素。其中有一个生动的场景涉及海量的血浆。“我们为此专门留出了一整周的时间，”她说，这对于节奏通常很快的电视剧来说极其罕见。这必须经过精确的计划和编排，不仅是因为卡德里尼在剧中的发色较浅，他们很快发现人造血浆把她的头发染成了粉红色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“甚至连那个人的脸脱落的镜头，也是在拍摄当天用义肢完成的，而不是靠CGI。你看到的就是实际呈现的效果，这有助于你的真实反应。”所以那不是后期制作完成的？“不是！他们用钓鱼线把它扯了下来。所以我也是在它剥落的那一刻第一次看到。它在我脑海里停留了好一会儿，因为它太恶心了。”事实证明，这是她最喜欢的亮点之一。“这实际上是我最喜欢该剧的片段之一。它就像一场血腥的歌剧。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《水晶湖》的到来伴随着新一波主流恐怖片浪潮，其中包括电影《迷恋》和《后室》，以及电视剧《魔女嘉莉》和《寡妇湾》。卡德里尼为什么认为恐怖片正迎来它的高光时刻？“这是一个很好的问题。我可以想象，这种体验本身带有一种强烈的当下感——而且这是一种可控的恐惧，因为你知道再过几个小时，事情就会尘埃落定。也许这更容易消化。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b046367ebe571c4cb882cf6692337411490afe5f/0_0_3600_2400/master/3600.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "乔·哈姆和琳达·卡德里尼在《广告狂人》中靠得很近，在餐厅桌旁专注交谈", "caption": "“相信我，这会变得非常精彩”……卡德里尼与乔·哈姆在《广告狂人》中。摄影：Everett Collection Inc/Alamy", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最近，卡德里尼在纽约动漫展的该剧展映活动后台。“现场有一些倒吸冷气、大喊和欢呼——随后是一阵笑声。那一刻你会觉得：‘好吧，这太棒了，因为这就是电影当年的效果。’它们让你感到害怕，然后你开怀大笑。这正是我们的目标。那种感觉真好。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡德里尼在加利福尼亚长大，于20世纪90年代中期开始演艺生涯。她的成名作是保罗·费格和贾德·阿帕图执导的青少年喜剧《怪胎与书呆子》，她在剧中饰演由乖变坏的女孩琳赛·韦尔。这部以20世纪80年代初为背景的剧集以充满温情和机智的视角展现了少年的叛逆，它曾如流星般短暂而耀眼，但在第一季播完之前就在2000年被NBC电视台迅速取消。除了卡德里尼，它还极大地推动了赛斯·罗根、杰森·席尔格和比茜·菲利普斯的演艺生涯。", "links": [{"text": "Freaks and Geeks", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2021/mar/22/freaks-and-geeks-hilarious-moving-and-endlessly-quotable-teen-show-for-the-ages"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“如果你的剧被砍了，你就彻底消失了，”她现在回忆道，“你甚至不知道它去了哪里。在我们不再制作它之后，它还能继续活下去的想法，在当时看来简直是不可能的。”然而，通过DVD和口碑传播，《平常与怪异》慢慢成为了高中校园题材电视剧中的经典。“它后来还能拥有生命力，这让人感到震惊——而它至今仍有生命力，那就更惊人了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/73adf7bea60f585add30a0d6ca92ab46233dc6a9/0_0_3000_1995/master/3000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "一个年轻女子和一个年轻男子坐在食堂桌旁，端着装有食物的餐盘正在交谈", "caption": "成名角色……卡德里尼与杰森·席格尔在《平常与怪异》中。摄影：All4", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "说起史上最伟大的电视剧集，卡德里尼在《广告狂人》第六季中加入了演员阵容，饰演与唐·德雷珀有染的西尔维娅·罗斯。当时保密工作极其严格，以至于她去试镜时，连名字和细节都被改掉了。“我根本不知道自己在演什么，[创作者]马修·维纳对我说：‘相信我，这会变得非常精彩。’我想我拿到最初的两份剧本时——里面只有一句台词。当时我想：‘我在干什么？这到底是什么？’”但维纳曾告诉她这会是一个极好的角色，而他并没有撒谎。她的角色不仅后来让唐想起了他年轻时的一名性工作者，还得以主动离开了他，从而引发了一场迷恋。“对我来说，这一切像个惊喜一样徐徐展开，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年9月，卡德里尼凭借在HBO剧集《DTF圣路易斯》中饰演的卡罗尔·洛夫-斯默尼奇，赢得了她的第一座艾美奖。“我以前也获得过提名，但获奖的感觉完全不同，”她说，“那是一个美妙的时刻。”《DTF圣路易斯》是一部独特的剧集：卡罗尔嫁给了美国手语翻译弗洛伊德，却与他的死党克拉克有染，克拉克是一名骑着一辆怪异自行车的电视气象员，喜欢在做爱时假装自己是机器人。卡德里尼最初听说这部剧时，以为自己知道这个故事会走向何方。“一个已婚夫妇和挚友之间的三角恋，然后某个人横死，”她回忆道，“但当我读了剧本后，我想：‘我从来没读过这样的东西。’每当我以为我知道它要往哪里发展时，它总是以一种美丽、细腻且极其人性化的方式走向另一个方向。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/63f1350bf3c07836340fa96eea27bf22d4e48951/0_0_1920_1280/master/1920.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "琳达·卡德里尼手里拎着购物袋，站在湿漉漉街道上停放的汽车之间，神情焦虑。", "caption": "卡德里尼在获得艾美奖的《DTF圣路易斯》中的角色造型。", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部剧是一部关于孤独的奇异而温柔的沉思录，带有不按常理出牌的特质。例如，卡罗尔是一名兼职棒球裁判。“自从我演了裁判之后，我遇到了好多人，他们告诉我他们其实也是裁判，而且都是你意想不到的人。此外，他们不得不经受的来自家长们的攻击也相当搞笑。”她现在还能去裁判一场比赛吗？“也许是少棒联盟吧。我不知道自己能不能应付那些家长！”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那座艾美奖奖杯现在摆在她家的壁炉架上。她第一次上电视是在1994年，当时她是益智节目《价格是对的》的一名参赛者。你可以在油管（YouTube）上看到那一幕——她当时赢得了一个壁炉。等等，这不可能是同一个壁炉吧？“但愿如此！我已经没有那个壁炉了，因为说来也巧，它在一次火灾中被烧毁了。”你在火灾里烧掉了一个壁炉？“我当时在工作，把很多东西都存放在仓库里。那个仓库着火了。”但她把它保留了很久吗？“哦，很多年、很多年、很多年。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年早些时候，卡德里尼拍摄了心理恐怖片《他们知道》（They Know），该片由比尔·哈德编剧、执导并主演。“这绝对是他极其非凡的视角，”她说，不愿透露太多细节，除了自己饰演他的前妻。然而，这并不是说卡德里尼拍了另一部恐怖片就意味着她进入了尖叫女王时代。“我喜欢不断变换，”她说，“我从《DTF》无缝切换到《水晶湖》，中间只隔了一周。这感觉像是一个巨大的急转弯。所以我们拭目以待接下来会发生什么。”她停顿了一下，补充道：“不过谁也说不准。”", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "‘T he first time I had the tooth in my hand,” says Linda Cardellini, “I thought, ‘Oh my God, this is what I’m doing.’” The star of Freaks and Geeks, ER, Dead to Me, Mad Men and DTF St Louis (for which she recently won an Emmy) is talking about her pivot towards full-blown horror. In Crystal Lake, the prequel to the Friday the 13th movies, Cardellini plays Pamela Voorhees, the original slasher of the 1980 film. The tooth, by the way, is human and gets embedded in Pam’s knuckle – until she yanks it out with a gruesome, revolting slurping sound.", "links": [{"text": "Mad Men", "url": "https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/mad-men-tv-series"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Casual filmgoers may associate Friday the 13th with Jason, the hockey-mask-wearing serial killer. But aficionados will know that Pam, Jason’s mother, is the villain of the first movie. “He didn’t even have the mask until the third movie,” says Cardellini, who has clearly done her homework. “Pam is the original killer, in vengeance of his death.” (There is some massaging of previous storylines in Crystal Lake, such as moving Jason’s drowning from the 1950s to the early 70s, but since the franchise is flexible enough to have sent Jason into space at one point, a bit of timeline tweaking feels fair game.)"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/77b9c82d286c77293e353d5b810f2188578d0b67/0_504_3857_3086/master/3857.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "Linda Cardellini smiles, posing with hands on hips in a white dress", "caption": "‘I like to change it up’ …  Linda Cardellini. article_text:
‘T he first time I had the tooth in my hand,” says Linda Cardellini, “I thought, ‘Oh my God, this is what I’m doing.’” The star of Freaks and Geeks, ER, Dead to Me, Mad Men and DTF St Louis (for which she recently won an Emmy) is talking about her pivot towards full-blown horror. In Crystal Lake, the prequel to the Friday the 13th movies, Cardellini plays Pamela Voorhees, the original slasher of the 1980 film. The tooth, by the way, is human and gets embedded in Pam’s knuckle – until she yanks it out with a gruesome, revolting slurping sound.

Casual filmgoers may associate Friday the 13th with Jason, the hockey-mask-wearing serial killer. But aficionados will know that Pam, Jason’s mother, is the villain of the first movie. “He didn’t even have the mask until the third movie,” says Cardellini, who has clearly done her homework. “Pam is the original killer, in vengeance of his death.” (There is some massaging of previous storylines in Crystal Lake, such as moving Jason’s drowning from the 1950s to the early 70s, but since the franchise is flexible enough to have sent Jason into space at one point, a bit of timeline tweaking feels fair game.)

The Friday the 13th franchise has a devoted audience – and Crystal Lake’s showrunner, Brad Caleb Kane, is among them. “He’s such a fan,” says Cardellini. “I felt he would have an idea of what fans were wanting.” Kane wrote the part specifically for her, after seeing her in Netflix thriller Dead to Me, which came as a surprise. “My biggest question was, ‘How did I become the person at the front of your mind for this?’” she laughs. Did they feel any pressure in taking Friday the 13th on? “It’s daunting, but hopefully it’s an opportunity to see more of something that didn’t really get its own avenue.”

Anyone who grew up in the 1980s and 90s, as Cardellini did (she is 51), will remember sleepovers with rented VHS tapes and a lot of screaming whenever Freddy Krueger, Michael Myers or Jason Voorhees appeared on screen. “It was forbidden fruit, almost,” she says. “You weren’t supposed to be able to watch it, but you would. And not only the gore but the sexuality – all the things you’re not supposed to be watching. I think it is part of the allure when you’re young. It seems off-limits and rebellious.”

She liked the jump scares and the gore, which is handy, because Crystal Lake is full of them. One vivid sequence involves an astronomical amount of blood. “We reserved a whole week for that,” she says, which is highly unusual for TV, as it tends to move quickly. It had to be precisely planned and choreographed, not least because Cardellini’s hair in the show is lighter, and they soon found that the fake blood stained it pink.

“Even the guy’s face coming off is done on the day with prosthetics, instead of CGI. It’s what you’re actually looking at, which helps with your reaction.” So that wasn’t done in post-production? “No! They pulled it off with fishing wire. So I saw it for the first time as it came off. It stuck with me for a while, because it’s disgusting .” It proved to be one of her highlights. “That’s actually one of my favourite parts of the show. It’s like a blood opera.”

Crystal Lake arrives on a new wave of mainstream horror, from films such as Obsession and Backrooms to Carrie and Widow’s Bay on TV. Why does Cardellini think horror is having a moment? “It’s a great question. I can imagine there’s something about the experience of it that is very present – and it’s a controlled fear, because you know that in a few hours, you will have a resolution. Maybe that is digestible.”

Recently, Cardellini was backstage at a screening of the show at New York Comic Con. “There was some gasping and yelling and cheers – and afterwards, a laugh. That’s when you’re like, ‘OK, this is great, because that’s what the movies did.’ They made you afraid, then you laughed out loud. That is what we were going for. That felt good.”

Cardellini grew up in California and started acting in the mid-1990s. Her breakout was Freaks and Geeks , the Paul Feig/Judd Apatow teen comedy in which she played good girl gone bad Lindsay Weir. The early 80s-set series, a fond, witty look at teenage rebellion, burned bright and fast and was promptly cancelled by NBC in 2000, before its first season had finished airing. As well as Cardellini, it rocket-launched the careers of Seth Rogen, Jason Segel and Busy Philipps.

“If you got cancelled, you were just gone ,” she says now. “You didn’t even know where it went. The idea that it would live on, once we weren’t going to make any more, just didn’t seem possible.” Through DVDs and word of mouth, though, Freaks and Geeks slowly became a classic of the high school TV genre. “That it had a life afterwards was a shock – and that it still has a life is amazing.”

On the subject of all-time-greatest TV series, Cardellini joined Mad Men in its sixth season, playing Sylvia Rosen, who has an affair with Don Draper. There was such secrecy around this that when she auditioned, names and details were changed. “I had no idea what I would be doing and [creator] Matt Weiner said, ‘Just trust me, it’s gonna get great.’ I think it was the first two scripts I got – I had one line. I thought, ‘What am I doing? What is this?’” But Weiner had told her it would be a great part and he was not lying. Not only does her character go on to remind Don of a sex worker from his youth, she also gets to leave him, triggering an obsession. “It unfolded like a surprise for me,” she says.

In September, Cardellini won her first Emmy for her role as Carol Love-Smernitch in HBO’s DTF St Louis. “I’ve been nominated before, but winning is a very different feeling,” she says. “It was a wonderful moment.” DTF St Louis is a singular series: Carol is married to American Sign Language interpreter Floyd, but is having an affair with his best friend Clark, a TV weatherman who rides a weird bike and likes to pretend to be a robot during sex. When Cardellini first heard about the show, she thought she knew how the story would go. “A love triangle between a married couple and a best friend, and somebody turns up dead,” she recalls. “But when I read it, I thought, ‘I’ve never read anything like this.’ Every time I thought I knew where it was going, it went somewhere else, in this beautiful, nuanced, very human way.”

The show is a strange, sweet meditation on loneliness, with an offbeat streak. Carol, for instance, is a part-time baseball umpire. “Since I’ve played an umpire, I’ve met so many people who have told me they are also umpires, and it’s people you don’t expect. Also, the parent attacks that they have to weather are pretty funny.” Could she still umpire a game? “Maybe Little League. I don’t know if I can handle the parents!”

That Emmy award now lives on the mantel of her fireplace. Her first appearance on TV was in 1994, when she was a contestant on the quizshow The Price Is Right. You can see it on YouTube – she won a fireplace. Hang on, it’s not the same fireplace is it? “I wish! I don’t have that fireplace any more because, oddly enough, I lost it in a fire.” You lost a fireplace in a fire? “I was working and put a lot of stuff in storage. The storage facility caught fire.” But she had kept it for a long time? “Oh, for years and years and years.”

Earlier this year, Cardellini filmed They Know, a psychological horror movie written and directed by Bill Hader, who also stars. “It’s definitely his incredibly extraordinary point of view,” she says, reluctant to give too much away beyond the fact she plays his ex-wife. The fact that it’s another horror does not mean, however, that Cardellini is in her scream queen era. “I like to change it up,” she says. “I went from DTF to Crystal Lake with one week in between. That seemed like a big left turn. So we’ll see what comes up.” She pauses and adds: “But you never know.”

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "在约翰内斯堡的 Bag Factory 艺术家工作室，“跨越边界成长：来自约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事”（Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories from Johannesburg & Beyond）通过年轻人的摄影和播客作品，探讨了移民、记录与归属感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在一个连获取教育、工作和出行自由都可能取决于一张纸的城市里长大，究竟意味着什么？通过影像、口述记录以及他们自己的策展选择，展览的参与者们审视了排斥现象，以及那些支撑他们前行的关系和日常空间。在接受 ART AFRICA 采访时，ERC 项目“跨越边界成长”（Growing Up Across Borders）首席研究员简·弗里德曼（Jane Freedman）反思了参与式研究、代表权的责任，以及年轻人对自己如何分享故事的主导权。本展览由欧洲研究理事会（European Research Council）在 ERC-AdG 101141171 资助下支持展出。“安全之地”（A Place of Safety）作者：露西亚（Lucia）。约翰内斯堡拉罗谢尔（La Rochelle）的老天主教堂。（该教堂对多种国籍开放，展现了人们之间的团结。）“跨越边界成长：来自约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事”，2026年。图片由 ERC 项目“跨越边界成长”提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/A-place-of-safety-1-773x1030.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "“安全之地”（A Place of Safety）作者：露西亚（Lucia）。约翰内斯堡拉罗谢尔（La Rochelle）的老天主教堂。（该教堂对多种国籍开放，展现了人们之间的团结。）“跨越边界成长：来自约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事”，2026年。图片由 ERC 项目“跨越边界成长”提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "布伦顿·贝尔-罗伯茨（Brendon Bell-Roberts）：“跨越边界成长”聚焦于年轻人在不同国家间应对流离失所、流动性以及向成年过渡的经历。是什么理念或问题塑造了将这些经历汇聚在一个展览中的策展方法？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "简·弗里德曼：“跨越边界成长”是一个国际研究项目，旨在弥补对青年移民和流动性理解中的关键空白，特别是在青年声音往往被忽视的强迫移民背景下。我们关注年轻人对移民、排斥和歧视的生活经验、知识、记忆、雄心和想象，同时也关注他们在收容国中进行抵抗、适应和归属的策略。在他们从童年过渡到成年这一人生的关键时期，他们是如何体验和理解流动与静止的？在开展研究时，我们始终力求与年轻人合作，而不仅仅是将年轻人当作纯粹的研究“对象”；这意味着年轻人是知识共同创造的核心合作者——从研究问题和方法的共同设计，到学术与非学术创意成果的共同制作。这个展览的想法是为我们一直合作的年轻人创造一个空间，让他们能够与更广泛的公众分享他们的照片和播客，从而传播他们创作的艺术和知识。我们认为，重要的不仅是让研究停留在大学或学术环境中，还要让公众更广泛地获取这些知识，并让知识的创造者即年轻人能够以他们希望的方式使用他们所制作的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "约翰内斯堡的分支是通过一个由年轻人讲述自身生活经历的参与式过程发展起来的。这种工作方式如何塑造了你对该项目中策展的理解？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我和我的研究同事格伦达·桑塔纳·德安德拉德（Glenda Santana de Andrade）和阿隆·特斯法伊（Aron Tesfai）认为，同样重要的是，要让参与项目的年轻人来主导展览的策展工作。这意味着在实践中，拍摄照片并撰写附带说明文字的年轻人，也带头组织他们的作品并策划展览。照片的所有选择以及将其分类并在展览中共同悬挂的组织工作，都是由年轻人自己完成的。因此，他们为自己将要展示的内容以及如何展示带来了另一层面的分析和意义。作为研究人员，有时我们很难不干涉这些策展选择，但我们认为，让参与者对自己作品的理解以及对其应如何被观看的理解占据主导地位，是非常重要的。“外国人的困难”（Foreigners' Difficulties）作者：洛伊索（Loyiso）。洛基（Rocky）的街道，由于没有所需的文件和许可证，店主们被迫关门以防被捕。“跨越边界成长：来自约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事”2026年。图片由 ERC 项目“跨越边界成长”提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Foreigners-difficulties--1030x773.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "“外国人的困难”（Foreigners' Difficulties）作者：洛伊索（Loyiso）。洛基（Rocky）的街道，由于没有所需的文件和许可证，店主们被迫关门以防被捕。“跨越边界成长：来自约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事”2026年。图片之光由 ERC 项目“跨越边界成长”提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "摄影和播客在整个展览中并行运作。是什么吸引你在展览空间中将视觉和口述叙事结合在一起？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们认为视觉和口述叙事是互补的，能带来不同的表达机会。在与年轻人的工作坊中，我们提供了摄影和播客这两种表达形式，以便他们探索讲述自身经历的不同方式。我们发现，摄影带来了更具“诗意”或艺术性的表达，展现了他们所面临的障碍、克服障碍的策略以及日常生活中各方面的快乐，而播客则让他们能够以更具政治性的方式参与到对歧视和仇外心理等问题的讨论中。使用这两种不同的表达方式，也让年轻参与者能够探索他们在表达方面的偏好、优势和劣势。正如其中一位年轻人所解释的那样：“摄影让我能够更好地表达生活在南非的移民的现实、挣扎与胜利，但同样也很简单地表达了这个国家的生活现实。摄影的优势之一，就是能够通过镜头表达自我（尤其是对害羞的人来说）。”我们觉得，在展览中将这两种叙事模式结合起来，是一种呈现年轻人经历和表达之全貌的方式，能让他们用不同的方式谈论自己的生活。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "许多参展艺术家都通过个人和日常经验来探讨身份、移民和归属感等问题。你是如何思考个人故事与更广泛的社会现实之间的关系的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们认为这些个人故事生动展现了由移民和难民政策、仇外心理以及歧视所构成的更广泛社会现实。汇集一系列个人经历的故事和图景，让我们得以理解这些年轻人的生活、身份以及归属感或疏离感，是如何受到其证件无法让他们接受高等教育，或是他们在获得医疗或就业机会时受到歧视等状况所支配的。这类个人故事汇聚在一起，便直指他们所面临的更广泛政治、经济和社会现实。另一方面，他们关于社区、友谊和安全空间的故事，则展现了移民在面对排挤时建立韧性、抵抗力和社区感这一更广泛的现实。“没有自由的梦想”作者：瓦达（Warda）。由于缺乏证件，人们不得不待在室内，无法工作，在外面还可能面临许多虐待。《跨越边境长大：约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事》，2026年。图片由“跨越边境长大”欧洲研究委员会项目提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Dreams-without-Freedom-1-1030x773.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "“没有自由的梦想”作者：瓦达（Warda）。由于缺乏证件，人们不得不待在室内，无法工作，在外面还可能面临许多虐待。《跨越边境长大：约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事》，2026年。图片由“跨越边境长大”欧洲研究委员会项目提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "身份证明文件既是摄影作品中的一个主题，也是塑造年轻人获取教育、流动性和机会之渠道的因素。展览是如何看待身份证明文件所承载的不同含义的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "身份证明文件是我们整个研究项目中一个突出的主题。获取证件的困难——无论是避难或难民许可，还是最终的永久居民身份——对这些年轻人来说都是一场持续的斗争。他们拥有或没有的证件类型，对其能做什么有着巨大的影响。他们能上学或上大学吗？能获得医疗服务吗？能找到工作吗？对一些人来说，缺乏证件还会让他们面临被捕甚至被驱逐出境的风险。因此，证件贯穿了他们作品的始终，有时被直观地描绘成一张A4纸，有时则更具隐喻性，表现出排挤、失落或重重阻碍。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参展的年轻人与约翰内斯堡有着不同的联系，包括在当地出生的人、迁居到此的人以及在不同文化之间成长的人。透过他们的视角，约翰内斯堡呈现出怎样的面貌？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这些年轻人眼中，约翰内斯堡是一座有着多重面孔和多重含义的城市。有些人选择展示这座城市中他们感到危险的区域，那里有移民开的店遭到袭击，或者移民居住在不卫生且危险的条件中。另一些人则展示了他们感到快乐和安全的地方，比如他们与朋友玩耍的运动场，以及那些能给予他们安心和快乐的自然场所。这些多重含义交织在他们对一座城市的体验中，他们在那里长大，学会了如何在其中生活，却有时又感到自己并不真正属于这里。“多样性中的团结”作者：科莱特（Collette）。孩子们没有歧视地一起玩耍，纯粹为了游戏的乐趣。尽管国籍不同，依然团结一心。《跨越边境长大：约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事》，2026年。图片由“跨越边境长大”欧洲研究委员会项目提供。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artafricamagazine.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Unity-in-Diversity--773x1030.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "“多样性中的团结”作者：科莱特（Collette）。孩子们没有歧视地一起玩耍，纯粹为了游戏的乐趣。尽管国籍不同，依然团结一心。《跨越边境长大：约翰内斯堡及其他地区的青年故事》，2026年。图片由“跨越边境长大”欧洲研究委员会项目提供。", "credit": "ART AFRICA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与那些将个人经历变成公开展览一部分的年轻人合作，引发了关于署名权和代表权的问题。在整个项目中你是如何处理这些问题的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们一直在探讨关于作者身份与表征的这些伦理和本体论问题，并与我们合作的年轻人进行了持续讨论。我们项目的一个核心原则是以参与式和非榨取式的方式工作，因此我们希望确保年轻人既是决定如何以及以何种形式表达自己的根源，也是决定如何分享其作品的决策者。我们与他们就公开展示其艺术作品的后果、这对他们意味着什么、优势以及可能存在的危险进行了长时间的讨论。这些作品是在一个国际研究项目（Growing Up Across Borders）的背景下创作的，但最终这些作品的作者身份和所有权属于这些年轻人，他们可以自行决定是否以及如何分享自己的艺术。", "links": [{"text": "Growing Up Across Borders", "url": "https://erc-grabs.univ-paris8.fr/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随着这些照片和声音从个人经验走向画廊的公共空间，您认为年轻的讲述者、他们的作品与观众之间的相遇会带来哪些可能性？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "看到观众与展览、与所分享的照片和声音以及与年轻艺术家本身产生互动的方式，我们深受鼓舞。对于观众而言，我们希望这能成为一种使他们对移民以及南非年轻难民经历的观点和理解更加细致入微的方式。通过与一些前来观展的观众的交流，我们发现他们此前并未完全意识到这些年轻人所面临的一些障碍和排斥，例如无法获得教育，而意识到这一点使他们对南非关于移民和难民的公众辩论与话语进行了反思。我们深知要大幅改变公众舆论是非常困难的，但希望对日常切身现实的更深入理解能够有助于推动实现更大的普遍包容并呼吁包容。对年轻人而言，展示其作品并与观众交流的机会同样非常重要。这让他们建立起信心，认识到自己的作品极具价值，足以在公共空间展出，并且人们希望看到他们的照片、聆听他们的播客。正如一位年轻女性向我们解释的那样：“看到我的照片以及上面的名字，这种感觉太棒了。人们询问图片说明，问我是什么意思。这是一种美妙的感觉。对我来说，交谈和辩论真的很难，要跟不认识的人说话；我在工作坊中获得的自信，我把它用在了展览中，向人们进行解释。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展览曾在约翰内斯堡纽顿（Newtown）的Bag Factory艺术家工作室（Bag Factory Artists’ Studio）展出，于2026年6月13日开幕。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
At Bag Factory Artists’ Studios in Johannesburg, ‘Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories from Johannesburg & Beyond’ explores migration, documentation and belonging through young people’s photographs and podcasts.

What does it mean to grow up in a city where access to education, work and movement can depend on a piece of paper? Through images, spoken accounts and their own curatorial choices, the exhibition’s participants examine exclusion alongside the relationships and everyday spaces that sustain them. In an interview with ART AFRICA , Jane Freedman, lead researcher for the ERC Project “Growing Up Across Borders”, reflects on participatory research, the responsibilities of representation, and young people’s authority over how they share their stories. This exhibition was financed by the European Research Council, under ERC-AdG 101141171. ‘A Place of Safety’ By Lucia. Old Catholic church, La Rochelle, Johannesburg. (Church open to many nationalities, showcasing unity among people.) Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories From Johannesburg & Beyond, 2026. Image Courtesy of ERC Project ‘Growing Up Across Borders.

Brendon Bell-Roberts: ‘Growing Up Across Borders’ centres on young people’s experiences navigating displacement, mobility, and the transition into adulthood across different countries. What ideas or questions shaped the curatorial approach to bringing these experiences together in one exhibition?

Jane Freedman: The Growing Up Across Borders project is an international research project which aims to bridge a critical gap in understanding youth migration and mobility, particularly in contexts of forced migration, where young people’s voices are often unheard. We focus on young individuals’ lived experiences, knowledge, memories, ambitions, and imaginaries of migration, of exclusion and discrimination, but also of strategies for resistance, for adaptation and belonging in host countries. At a critical time in their lives, moving from childhood to adulthood, how do they experience and understand mobility and immobility?. In carrying out our research, we always strive to work with youth, and not just on youth as mere “subjects” of study; this means young people are central collaborators in the co-creation of knowledge – from the co-design of research questions and methods, to the co-production of academic and non-academic creative output. The idea of this exhibition was to create a space for the young people we have been working with to share their photographs and podcasts with a wider public and thus to disseminate the art and the knowledge that they had created. We feel that it is important that research does not stay within a university or academic setting but is made more widely available to the public and that those who created the knowledge, i.e., the young people, can use what they have made in a way that they wish.

The Johannesburg chapter developed through a participatory process in which young people narrate their own lived experiences. How did this way of working shape your understanding of curating in the project?

Together with my fellow researchers, Glenda Santana de Andrade and Aron Tesfai, we felt that it was important to allow the young people taking part in the project to lead the curation of the exhibition as well. This meant in practice that the young people who took the photographs and wrote the captions that accompany them also took the lead in organising their work and curating the exhibition. All of the selection and organisation of the photographs into categories which would be hung together in the exhibition was done by the young people themselves. They thus brought another level of analysis and meaning to what they would be showing and how they would be exhibiting it. As researchers, we sometimes found it hard not to intervene in these curatorial choices, but we thought it was very important that we should allow the participants’ own understanding of their work and of how it should be seen to take precedence. ‘Foreigners’ Difficulties’ By Loyiso. The streets of Rocky, where shop owners were forced to close their shops as to not get arrested, due to not having the required documentation and permits. Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories From Johannesburg & Beyond 2026. Image Courtesy of ERC Project ‘Growing Up Across Borders.

Photography and podcasting operate alongside one another throughout the exhibition. What drew you to bringing visual and spoken storytelling into conversation in the exhibition space?

We feel that visual and spoken storytelling are complementary and bring different opportunities for expression. During our workshops with the young people, we offered both forms of expression – through photography and through podcasting – so that they could explore varying ways of narrating their experiences. We found that whilst the photography brought more “poetic” or artistic expressions of the barriers they face, as well as their strategies for overcoming these and their joys in various facets of their everyday lives, the podcasts allowed them to engage in a more political way with questions of discrimination and xenophobia, for example. Using the two different methods of expression also allowed the young participants to explore their preferences and strengths and weaknesses in terms of expression. As one of the young people explains: “Photography has allowed me to better express the reality, the struggles, and the triumphs of immigrants living in South Africa, but also, quite simply, the realities of life in this country. One of the advantages of photography is the ability to express oneself through the lens (especially for shy people).” Bringing these two modes of narration together during the exhibition was, we felt, a way to present a more complete picture of the young people’s experiences and expressions, and to allow them different ways to talk about their lives.

Many of the participating artists approach questions of identity, migration and belonging through personal and everyday experiences. How did you think about the relationship between individual stories and wider social realities?

We think that these individual stories illustrate wider social realities structured by immigration and refugee policies, xenophobia and discrimination. Bringing together a range of stories and illustrations of individual experiences allows us to understand how these young people’s lives, identities and feelings of belonging or non-belonging are structured by the ways in which their documentation does not allow them to access higher education, or the ways that they are discriminated against in access to health or employment. These types of individual stories, when taken together, talk to wider political, economic and social realities which they are facing. On the other hand, their stories of community, friendship, and spaces of safety speak to a wider reality for migrants of creating spaces of resilience and resistance of community in the face of exclusion. ‘Dreams Without Freedom’ By Warda. Due to lack of documentation, one has to stay indoors, cannot work, and may face a lot of abuse outside. Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories From Johannesburg & Beyond, 2026. Image Courtesy of ERC Project ‘Growing Up Across Borders.

Documentation appears both as a subject within the photographs and as something that can shape a young person’s access to education, movement and opportunity. How does the exhibition approach the different meanings documentation can carry?

Documentation is a theme which has featured prominently throughout our research project. The difficulties of obtaining documentation – whether it be an asylum or refugee permit, or even eventually permanent residence status – are a constant struggle for these young people. And the types of documentation they have or don’t have have a huge impact on what they can do. Can they go to school or university? Access health services? Find a job? For some, a lack of documentation also leads to vulnerability to arrest or eventually deportation. So documentation is a constant thread throughout their works, sometimes portrayed literally as a piece of A4 paper, sometimes more metaphorically, showing exclusion, loss or barriers.

The exhibition brings together young people with different relationships to Johannesburg, including those born in the city, those who migrated there and those growing up between cultures. Through their perspectives, how does Johannesburg emerge?

Johannesburg emerges as a city with multiple faces and multiple meanings for these young people. Some have chosen to show areas of the city where they feel they are in danger, where migrant businesses have been attacked, or where migrants are housed in insalubrious and dangerous conditions. Others have shown places where they feel happy and safe, such as sports grounds where they play with friends, places where nature reassures them and makes them feel happy. These multiple meanings are present in their experiences of a city where they have grown up, and which they have learned to navigate, whilst sometimes feeling that they do not really belong. ‘Unity in Diversity’ By Collette. Children playing together without discrimination, for the fun of the game. Togetherness despite being different nationalities. Growing Up Across Borders: Youth Stories From Johannesburg & Beyond, 2026. Image Courtesy of ERC Project ‘Growing Up Across Borders.

Working with young people whose personal experiences become part of a public exhibition raises questions around authorship and representation. How did you approach these questions throughout the project?

We are constantly engaging with these ethical and ontological questions about authorship and representation, and discuss them constantly with the young people with whom we work. A core principle of our project is to work in a way which is participatory and non-extractivist, so that we wish to ensure that the young people are at the root both of deciding how and in what form to express themselves, and also deciding how their productions will be shared. We have had long discussions with them around the repercussions of sharing their art in a public space, what it means for them, the advantages and also the possible dangers. These works were produced in the context of an international research project ( Growing Up Across Borders ), but ultimately the authorship and ownership of the works is that of the young people, and it is up to them to decide if and how they wish to share their art.

As these photographs and voices move from personal experience into the public space of the gallery, what possibilities do you see emerging from the encounter between the young storytellers, their work and audiences?

We have been encouraged to see the ways in which the audiences have engaged with the exhibition, with the photographs and voices which are shared, but also with the young artists themselves. For audiences, we hope that this may be a way to nuance opinions and understandings of migration and of the experiences of young refugees in South Africa. From discussions with some of those audience members who have come to see the exhibition, we have found out that they had not been fully aware of some of the barriers and exclusions that these young people face, for example, not being able to access education, and that becoming aware of these has made them reflect on the public debates and discourses around migrants and refugees in South Africa. We are aware that it is very hard to shift public opinion in a major way, but hopefully a greater understanding of daily lived realities like this can help to move towards a greater general tolerance and push for inclusion. For the young people also, the opportunity to show their work and to engage with audiences has been very important. It has given them confidence to know that their work is valuable enough to be exhibited in public spaces and that people want to see their photographs and listen to their podcasts. As one young woman explained to us: “It was great to see my pictures, my name on them. People asked about the captions, what I meant by it. It was a great feeling. Talking and having debates was really hard to me, to talk to people that I do not know; the confidence that I got at the workshop I used it in the exhibition to explain to people.”

This exhibition was on view at Bag Factory Artists’ Studio in Newtown, Johannesburg, opening on 13 June 2026.

article_text:
Provo, Utah-based genre festival FilmQuest is detailing its inaugural film market .

Named the “ Marché du Cthulhu ” in tribute to H.P. Lovecraft’s famed cosmic beast, the market is described as “taking a curated approach to presenting buyers, distributors, sales agents, and more with films they believe have commercial value and that will sell in markets around the world along with the festival’s Official Competition lineup.”

Related Stories

Netflix Touts International Success Amid Content Leadership Shake-Up, Eyes More Broadcaster Deals After TF1 and Globo Pacts

Why Did Netflix Boot Bela Bajaria?

The market takes place in person and remotely, concurrent with the festival, from Oct. 27 — 29, at Provo’s InTension Studios, hosted by the genre production company Intension Industries.

“We’re thrilled to have an opportunity to provide exposure for an additional collection of features. As the appetite for genre titles continues to expand, we see this market leading to more acquisitions in the space. More support for emerging filmmakers translates to more content offerings for audiences,” Jon Fitzgerald, Marché du Cthulhu director and co-founder, said in a statement.

“We received 3,000 submissions this season for FilmQuest, nearly 500 of which were feature films,” Jonathan Martin, festival director and Marché co-founder, also said in a statement. “While it would be impossible for us to program all of them in our competition lineup, we saw many feature films that have commercial value that still deserved to be recognized and seen by distributors that are potentially being overlooked.”

Participants include Sony, CAA, Vertical Entertainment, Bleecker Street, Scatena & Rosner Films, Breaking Glass, StudioDome, Chroma, Archstone, Buffalo 8 and Jackrabbit Media with more to be announced.

In addition to the available Official Selection films, available titles include Guy Bauer’s dark comedy thriller “Ana the Cleaner” (USA); Andy Chen’s sci-fi thriller “Another” (USA); Julian Hoffman’s horror slasher comedy “Autumn Hill” (Canada); Jesse Behrenwald’s sci-fi thriller “Brother Saves Us” (USA); Cyrus Neshvad’s dystopian horror, and Luxembourg’s official Oscar entry, “Child” (Luxembourg); Stewart Sparke’s sci-fi creature feature “Dead Reset” (United Kingdom); David Hebero’s familial horror “House of Atreus” (Spain); Jen Walden’s postapocalyptic sci-fi “Lumi” (Canada); Jessica Vogt’s space-set sci-fi “Phase” (United Kingdom); Robert Cannon’s action thriller “Prowler” (USA); Rob Alicea’s sci-fi screen-life thriller “Serena” (USA); Willard Morgan’s and Gideon Berger’s period horror “The Tannery” (USA); Shayne Putzlocher’s horror “The Wrath” (Canada); Maxwell Morro’s action folk horror “Valley of the Horntak” (USA); and Nick Psinakis’s and Kevin Ignatius 70s set crime thriller “Valley View Motel” (USA).

“Every season, there’s at least an additional 30-50 titles submitted to the festival which aren’t programmed that we later see being distributed across various platforms,” Martin also said. “The thinking is that if we’re already watching hundreds of the latest genre features on the market, which gives us an early look at all the trends, emerging talent, and then some, why not hone that down and present this directly to the buyers with a market experience that doesn’t involve hundreds of booths, thousands of films, and all the pomp and circumstance that comes with it, but instead pare it down to films we know will sell and whose value to the market are immediately obvious.”

The team is already looking to grow the market next year, hoping to include competitions, pitch opportunities and an expanded lineup.

title_original: Papel e projeção: aproximações e distâncias entre fotolivros e fotofilmes
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/4000-disparos_6.jpg?resize=1024%2C432&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "Frame de 4.000 disparos , de Jonathas de Andrade, 2010, vídeo-filme em super-8 digitalizado em HD.", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A história das imagens técnicas no século 20 é também a história de suas contaminações. Fotografia e cinema, embora tratados como campos distintos, desenvolveram-se em permanente diálogo, compartilhando dispositivos, procedimentos e modos de ver. Já no século 19, a busca pela captura do movimento levou à convergência entre imagem fixa e animada, culminando no cinema, e essa relação só se intensificou ao longo do século 20, sobretudo em contextos experimentais e artísticos, nos quais as fronteiras entre meios se tornaram cada vez mais porosas."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "No Brasil, a década de 1970 marca um momento decisivo para a expansão dessas linguagens híbridas, com a produção de audiovisuais com diapositivos. A ausência da tecnologia digital tornava essas práticas complexas e exigentes: os audiovisuais utilizavam projetores de slides sincronizados a fitas cassete, o que influenciava diretamente a estética das obras — tempos mais homogêneos, montagem mais rígida, menor liberdade de manipulação. Já os fotofilmes eram realizados literalmente filmando fotografias impressas e ampliadas em mesas de trucagem, atendendo também pelo nome de cinema de animação, com panorâmicas e zooms produzidos pela câmera cinematográfica sobre imagens estáticas, para criar a ilusão de deslocamento."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "É nesse contexto que podemos pensar o fotofilme: uma obra audiovisual construída a partir de imagens estáticas organizadas em sequência, às quais se somam recursos da montagem cinematográfica — cortes secos, transições, duração, banda sonora como música incidental, silêncio, narração e ruídos. É, como costumo dizer, uma linguagem com “cara de cinema e corpo de fotografia”."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "O fotofilme ocupa uma fronteira inquietante entre dois regimes de imagem. Enquanto o cinema é fluxo contínuo e presentificação do tempo, a fotografia é o instante petrificado, associado à memória, à ausência e à suspensão. O fotofilme opera justamente nesse intervalo, mantendo a força contemplativa da fotografia, mas organizando as imagens segundo uma montagem temporal cinematográfica — como nos clássicos La Jetée (1962), de Chris Marker, ou em À João Guimarães Rosa (1969), de Marcello Tassara, realizado a partir das imagens de Maureen Bisilliat."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As aproximações entre fotofilmes e fotolivros tornam-se evidentes nos processos de edição. Em ambos, a narrativa nasce da relação entre as imagens: aproximações formais por cor, luz ou escala; construções temporais lineares ou fragmentadas; relações por simbolismo ou contraste. Como observa o fotógrafo, editor e curador Eder Chiodetto, organizar um conjunto de imagens implica estabelecer relações, ritmos, contiguidades e rupturas — a edição não é uma etapa posterior à produção das fotografias, mas uma operação que participa da construção narrativa e da produção de sentidos."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mas as diferenças entre eles são evidentes. O fotolivro é um objeto físico, palpável, com peso, textura, cheiro e volume. Sua narrativa é construída não apenas pelas imagens, mas pelo próprio corpo do livro: formato, papel, escala, gramatura, encadernação, acabamento e disposição das imagens participam ativamente da construção de sentido. O livro não é apenas o suporte que contém as fotografias: sua materialidade é parte essencial da obra."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Já o fotofilme é uma obra imaterial, um feixe de luz organizado no tempo. O autor define a duração de cada imagem, as transições, os possíveis reenquadramentos e a banda sonora. Diferentemente das imagens silenciosas do fotolivro, o fotofilme pode produzir imagens atravessadas por vozes, ruídos, música e mesmo silêncio, e o espectador é conduzido por um tempo previamente estabelecido e pela experiência sonora. A escala de sua exibição vai depender do dispositivo de projeção."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/4000-disparos_1.jpg?resize=1024%2C650&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "Frame de 4.000 disparos , de Jonathas de Andrade, 2010, vídeo-filme em super-8 digitalizado em HD.", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Montagem, duração e experiência"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sergei Eisenstein nos diz que a montagem não consiste apenas em organizar imagens sucessivas, mas em produzir relações e conflitos entre elas: o sentido pode nascer do encontro, do choque ou da aproximação entre imagens, e não apenas de cada imagem isolada. A montagem transforma a sucessão de imagens em pensamento."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Essa concepção é produtiva para pensar tanto o fotolivro quanto o fotofilme, pois, em ambos, o sentido se constrói também na relação entre as imagens. Uma fotografia pode modificar aquilo que percebemos na anterior, criar uma associação inesperada, estabelecer continuidade ou produzir contraste. No fotolivro, essas relações se dão principalmente pela proximidade espacial e pelo percurso do olhar entre as páginas. No fotofilme, elas se constituem também pela sucessão e pelo intervalo: uma imagem deixa de estar diante de nós, mas continua atuando sobre a percepção da imagem seguinte. A montagem acontece, assim, não apenas entre as imagens, mas também no espaço de relação que se abre entre elas."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Se Eisenstein pensa a montagem como relação e conflito, Andrei Tarkovski desloca a questão para a experiência do tempo: o cinema trabalha não só com a sucessão de imagens, mas com a duração que se acumula dentro do filme. Isso importa para o fotofilme porque a fotografia, embora fixa, passa a existir dentro de uma duração — dois segundos permitem apenas um reconhecimento imediato; vinte segundos podem transformar a observação em espera ou contemplação."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "É nesse sentido que 4000 disparos , de Jonathas de Andrade, torna-se um exemplo particularmente significativo. O artista viaja pela América Latina “para um reconhecimento de território, partindo de um sentimento de amnésia histórica” fotografando homens anônimos pelas ruas. O fotolivro reúne esses retratos onde podemos observar claramente cada rosto apresentado no formato 10x13cm. Na versão audiovisual, as fotografias aparentemente destinadas à contemplação são submetidas a uma sucessão extremamente rápida — os rostos aparecem e desaparecem antes que possamos nos deter sobre cada um deles. A fotografia continua fixa, mas sua experiência é transformada pela duração: o que está em jogo já não é apenas o que cada fotografia mostra, mas o tempo que temos, ou não temos, para olhar. A obra evidencia que a fotografia não precisa se movimentar para adquirir dimensão temporal — é o tempo de permanência na tela e a presença de sons distintos e até perturbadores que transformam a experiência fotográfica. Além disso, a escala da projeção pode ser muito maior que o formato diminuto do impresso. No fotolivro podemos nos demorar em cada rosto, enquanto no fotofilme a edição frenética nos permite ver por poucos segundos apenas alguns rostos previamente escolhidos pelo artista."}, {"type": Nos dois formatos, a imagem inteira só é revelada no final. No audiovisual o texto é narrado acrescido portanto do tom de voz e da emoção da leitura. Na peça impressa, ele se torna parte da imagem, sendo inserido na parte inferior das páginas. Isso é potente no fotofilme, em que uma fotografia pode ser acompanhada por sons que não necessariamente ilustram a imagem — o som pode introduzir uma dimensão ausente, fazendo existir um espaço fora de campo ou uma memória que a fotografia, sozinha, não produziria. Já Michel Chion, compositor e teórico, aprofunda essa relação ao pensar o audiovisual como uma experiência na qual vemos e ouvimos de maneira integrada: o som modifica a percepção da imagem, assim como a imagem transforma aquilo que ouvimos. Ele chama essa operação de audiovisão. A mesma fotografia pode adquirir sentidos diferentes dependendo do que ouvimos — uma voz pode transformar uma paisagem em lembrança; um ruído, introduzir tensão; o silêncio, produzir suspensão. A primeira edição do fotolivro autopublicado em 2012 se encontra esgotada e virou peça de colecionador. Partindo de um programa espacial da Zâmbia dos anos 1960, Middel constrói uma narrativa ficcional por meio de fotografias e documentos fictícios, evidenciando como a fotografia pode funcionar não apenas como registro, mas como matéria para construir ficção. No fotolivro, tipos distintos de papéis são usados. Papel jornal, couchê e vegetal se intercalam, aludindo a uma separação entre “fato” e “ficção”. A capa flexível é fechada por um elástico assemelhando-se a uma pasta de documentos. Quando as imagens de Middel são deslocadas para o audiovisual, se juntam a imagens documentais em movimento e o som passa a participar ativamente dessa construção: uma voz é adicionada trazendo um trecho de uma entrevista com o criador do programa espacial, uma música cria uma atmosfera, sons de elefantes entram em cena. É nesse sentido que Bresson e Chion são fundamentais para o fotofilme — fotografia, som e duração deixam de operar separadamente e passam a constituir, juntos, a experiência audiovisual."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As perspectivas de Eisenstein, Tarkovski, Bresson e Chion ajudam a compreender por que o fotofilme não é simplesmente uma sequência de fotografias colocadas em movimento e sonorizada ao acaso. O que se transforma não é a fotografia em si, mas o seu regime de existência: ela passa a estar submetida a uma duração, a uma montagem e a uma relação com o som — podendo esperar, desaparecer, retornar, entrar em conflito com outra imagem. Um fotofilme propõe uma experiência em que imagem, som e duração produzem sentidos conjuntamente."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "No fotolivro, por outro lado, a fotografia pode ser atravessada por uma página, interrompida por uma dobra ou fisicamente perfurada, como em Eu sabia . O livro pode fazer da própria matéria — papel, corte, vazio, escala, textura, encadernação — uma dimensão da montagem."}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Fotolivro The Afronauts , de Cristina de Middel, 2012. O fotolivro negocia o tempo da imagem através do gesto, do olhar e da materialidade do objeto; o fotofilme constrói uma temporalidade em que a fotografia é submetida à duração, à montagem e ao som. Mas ambos partem de uma mesma sequência de operações: selecionar, relacionar e apresentar imagens. É nesse território compartilhado que fotolivros e fotofilmes podem ser pensados como formas distintas de fazer a fotografia existir em relação, deixando de ser um instante isolado para se tornar sequência, duração, matéria, som e montagem. ///"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Claudia Tavares é artista visual e trabalha principalmente com fotografia e vídeo, em diálogo com desenhos. Já no século 19, a busca pela captura do movimento levou à convergência entre imagem fixa e animada, culminando no cinema, e essa relação só se intensificou ao longo do século 20, sobretudo em contextos experimentais e artísticos, nos quais as fronteiras entre meios se tornaram cada vez mais porosas.

No Brasil, a década de 1970 marca um momento decisivo para a expansão dessas linguagens híbridas, com a produção de audiovisuais com diapositivos. A ausência da tecnologia digital tornava essas práticas complexas e exigentes: os audiovisuais utilizavam projetores de slides sincronizados a fitas cassete, o que influenciava diretamente a estética das obras — tempos mais homogêneos, montagem mais rígida, menor liberdade de manipulação. Já os fotofilmes eram realizados literalmente filmando fotografias impressas e ampliadas em mesas de trucagem, atendendo também pelo nome de cinema de animação, com panorâmicas e zooms produzidos pela câmera cinematográfica sobre imagens estáticas, para criar a ilusão de deslocamento.

É nesse contexto que podemos pensar o fotofilme: uma obra audiovisual construída a partir de imagens estáticas organizadas em sequência, às quais se somam recursos da montagem cinematográfica — cortes secos, transições, duração, banda sonora como música incidental, silêncio, narração e ruídos. É, como costumo dizer, uma linguagem com “cara de cinema e corpo de fotografia”.

O fotofilme ocupa uma fronteira inquietante entre dois regimes de imagem. Enquanto o cinema é fluxo contínuo e presentificação do tempo, a fotografia é o instante petrificado, associado à memória, à ausência e à suspensão. O fotofilme opera justamente nesse intervalo, mantendo a força contemplativa da fotografia, mas organizando as imagens segundo uma montagem temporal cinematográfica — como nos clássicos La Jetée (1962), de Chris Marker, ou em À João Guimarães Rosa (1969), de Marcello Tassara, realizado a partir das imagens de Maureen Bisilliat.

As aproximações entre fotofilmes e fotolivros tornam-se evidentes nos processos de edição. Em ambos, a narrativa nasce da relação entre as imagens: aproximações formais por cor, luz ou escala; construções temporais lineares ou fragmentadas; relações por simbolismo ou contraste. Como observa o fotógrafo, editor e curador Eder Chiodetto, organizar um conjunto de imagens implica estabelecer relações, ritmos, contiguidades e rupturas — a edição não é uma etapa posterior à produção das fotografias, mas uma operação que participa da construção narrativa e da produção de sentidos.

Mas as diferenças entre eles são evidentes. O fotolivro é um objeto físico, palpável, com peso, textura, cheiro e volume. Sua narrativa é construída não apenas pelas imagens, mas pelo próprio corpo do livro: formato, papel, escala, gramatura, encadernação, acabamento e disposição das imagens participam ativamente da construção de sentido. O livro não é apenas o suporte que contém as fotografias: sua materialidade é parte essencial da obra.

Já o fotofilme é uma obra imaterial, um feixe de luz organizado no tempo. O autor define a duração de cada imagem, as transições, os possíveis reenquadramentos e a banda sonora. Diferentemente das imagens silenciosas do fotolivro, o fotofilme pode produzir imagens atravessadas por vozes, ruídos, música e mesmo silêncio, e o espectador é conduzido por um tempo previamente estabelecido e pela experiência sonora. A escala de sua exibição vai depender do dispositivo de projeção.

Montagem, duração e experiência

Sergei Eisenstein nos diz que a montagem não consiste apenas em organizar imagens sucessivas, mas em produzir relações e conflitos entre elas: o sentido pode nascer do encontro, do choque ou da aproximação entre imagens, e não apenas de cada imagem isolada. A montagem transforma a sucessão de imagens em pensamento.

Essa concepção é produtiva para pensar tanto o fotolivro quanto o fotofilme, pois, em ambos, o sentido se constrói também na relação entre as imagens. Uma fotografia pode modificar aquilo que percebemos na anterior, criar uma associação inesperada, estabelecer continuidade ou produzir contraste. No fotolivro, essas relações se dão principalmente pela proximidade espacial e pelo percurso do olhar entre as páginas. No fotofilme, elas se constituem também pela sucessão e pelo intervalo: uma imagem deixa de estar diante de nós, mas continua atuando sobre a percepção da imagem seguinte. A montagem acontece, assim, não apenas entre as imagens, mas também no espaço de relação que se abre entre elas.

Se Eisenstein pensa a montagem como relação e conflito, Andrei Tarkovski desloca a questão para a experiência do tempo: o cinema trabalha não só com a sucessão de imagens, mas com a duração que se acumula dentro do filme. Isso importa para o fotofilme porque a fotografia, embora fixa, passa a existir dentro de uma duração — dois segundos permitem apenas um reconhecimento imediato; vinte segundos podem transformar a observação em espera ou contemplação.

É nesse sentido que 4000 disparos , de Jonathas de Andrade, torna-se um exemplo particularmente significativo. O artista viaja pela América Latina “para um reconhecimento de território, partindo de um sentimento de amnésia histórica” fotografando homens anônimos pelas ruas. O fotolivro reúne esses retratos onde podemos observar claramente cada rosto apresentado no formato 10x13cm. Na versão audiovisual, as fotografias aparentemente destinadas à contemplação são submetidas a uma sucessão extremamente rápida — os rostos aparecem e desaparecem antes que possamos nos deter sobre cada um deles. A fotografia continua fixa, mas sua experiência é transformada pela duração: o que está em jogo já não é apenas o que cada fotografia mostra, mas o tempo que temos, ou não temos, para olhar. A obra evidencia que a fotografia não precisa se movimentar para adquirir dimensão temporal — é o tempo de permanência na tela e a presença de sons distintos e até perturbadores que transformam a experiência fotográfica. Além disso, a escala da projeção pode ser muito maior que o formato diminuto do impresso. No fotolivro podemos nos demorar em cada rosto, enquanto no fotofilme a edição frenética nos permite ver por poucos segundos apenas alguns rostos previamente escolhidos pelo artista.

Eisenstein e Tarkovski oferecem, assim, duas entradas complementares para compreender a montagem no fotofilme: a montagem como relação entre imagens e a montagem como construção de uma experiência temporal.

Não precisamos estabelecer uma oposição rígida entre fotolivro e fotofilme, como se o primeiro pertencesse ao espaço e o segundo ao tempo. A duração também está presente na leitura do fotolivro, mas, nesse caso, o leitor pode decidir quanto tempo permanecer diante de uma imagem, avançar, retornar ou interromper a sequência. No fotofilme, a duração é determinada pela montagem, embora a experiência doméstica permita pausá-lo, voltar ou revê-lo. Na sala de cinema, essa possibilidade de intervenção desaparece, e o espectador acompanha uma duração compartilhada e previamente estabelecida pela obra. Mais do que opor espaço e tempo, portanto, interessa perceber diferentes modos de construir e experimentar a duração das imagens.

O palpável e o incorpóreo

Se a duração permite aproximar fotolivros e fotofilmes, a materialidade evidencia uma distância fundamental entre os dois dispositivos.

Em Eu sabia , fotolivro e fotofilme de minha autoria, essa diferença torna-se particularmente evidente. Ambos foram construídos com uma única imagem que se desdobra em recortes e um texto relato questionando o poder de memória atribuído à fotografia. Nos dois formatos, a imagem inteira só é revelada no final. O fotolivro possui lacunas, buracos físicos abertos em algumas páginas, criando uma espécie de labirinto relacionado fisicamente às páginas seguintes. Essa operação não pode ser transposta para o fotofilme: no audiovisual podemos produzir a sensação de ausência por meio da montagem, pelo silêncio, mas não existe ali o gesto físico de perfurar uma folha. No fotolivro, a lacuna não é apenas representada: ela existe materialmente. Já no fotofilme, a imagem não pode ser tocada pelo espectador; é incorpórea ao tato, seu corpo é um feixe de luz. No audiovisual o texto é narrado acrescido portanto do tom de voz e da emoção da leitura. Na peça impressa, ele se torna parte da imagem, sendo inserido na parte inferior das páginas. A passagem de um meio a outro não significa apenas mudar a forma de apresentação, mas nesse caso, transformar as condições de experiência de uma mesma fotografia.

O som e a imagem

O pensamento sobre a duração da fotografia conduz ainda a outra dimensão fundamental do fotofilme: o som.

Robert Bresson, cineasta francês, é referência importante para pensar essa relação: o som não é um mero complemento daquilo que a imagem mostra, mas pode acrescentar uma informação invisível ou fazer imaginar aquilo que permanece fora do campo visual. Isso é potente no fotofilme, em que uma fotografia pode ser acompanhada por sons que não necessariamente ilustram a imagem — o som pode introduzir uma dimensão ausente, fazendo existir um espaço fora de campo ou uma memória que a fotografia, sozinha, não produziria. Já Michel Chion, compositor e teórico, aprofunda essa relação ao pensar o audiovisual como uma experiência na qual vemos e ouvimos de maneira integrada: o som modifica a percepção da imagem, assim como a imagem transforma aquilo que ouvimos. Ele chama essa operação de audiovisão. A mesma fotografia pode adquirir sentidos diferentes dependendo do que ouvimos — uma voz pode transformar uma paisagem em lembrança; um ruído, introduzir tensão; o silêncio, produzir suspensão. O som não é, portanto, uma camada adicionada depois: participa da própria construção da imagem no tempo.

É nesse ponto que The Afronauts , de Cristina de Middel, pode ser incorporado à discussão. A primeira edição do fotolivro autopublicado em 2012 se encontra esgotada e virou peça de colecionador. Partindo de um programa espacial da Zâmbia dos anos 1960, Middel constrói uma narrativa ficcional por meio de fotografias e documentos fictícios, evidenciando como a fotografia pode funcionar não apenas como registro, mas como matéria para construir ficção. No fotolivro, tipos distintos de papéis são usados. Papel jornal, couchê e vegetal se intercalam, aludindo a uma separação entre “fato” e “ficção”. A capa flexível é fechada por um elástico assemelhando-se a uma pasta de documentos. Quando as imagens de Middel são deslocadas para o audiovisual, se juntam a imagens documentais em movimento e o som passa a participar ativamente dessa construção: uma voz é adicionada trazendo um trecho de uma entrevista com o criador do programa espacial, uma música cria uma atmosfera, sons de elefantes entram em cena. É nesse sentido que Bresson e Chion são fundamentais para o fotofilme — fotografia, som e duração deixam de operar separadamente e passam a constituir, juntos, a experiência audiovisual.

As perspectivas de Eisenstein, Tarkovski, Bresson e Chion ajudam a compreender por que o fotofilme não é simplesmente uma sequência de fotografias colocadas em movimento e sonorizada ao acaso. O que se transforma não é a fotografia em si, mas o seu regime de existência: ela passa a estar submetida a uma duração, a uma montagem e a uma relação com o som — podendo esperar, desaparecer, retornar, entrar em conflito com outra imagem. Um fotofilme propõe uma experiência em que imagem, som e duração produzem sentidos conjuntamente.

No fotolivro, por outro lado, a fotografia pode ser atravessada por uma página, interrompida por uma dobra ou fisicamente perfurada, como em Eu sabia . O livro pode fazer da própria matéria — papel, corte, vazio, escala, textura, encadernação — uma dimensão da montagem.

Talvez seja justamente aí que a distância entre fotolivro e fotofilme se torne mais produtiva. Não se trata de hierarquizá-los, nem de dizer que um é mais temporal ou narrativo que o outro, mas de perceber que cada formato oferece modos diferentes de organizar relações entre imagem, tempo, matéria e som, produzindo experiências distintas para os espectadores. O fotolivro negocia o tempo da imagem através do gesto, do olhar e da materialidade do objeto; o fotofilme constrói uma temporalidade em que a fotografia é submetida à duração, à montagem e ao som. Mas ambos partem de uma mesma sequência de operações: selecionar, relacionar e apresentar imagens. É nesse território compartilhado que fotolivros e fotofilmes podem ser pensados como formas distintas de fazer a fotografia existir em relação, deixando de ser um instante isolado para se tornar sequência, duração, matéria, som e montagem. ///

Claudia Tavares é artista visual e trabalha principalmente com fotografia e vídeo, em diálogo com desenhos. É professora de linguagens visuais, orientadora de projetos, criadora do canal Fotofilmes no YouTube e pesquisa sobre fotofilmes desde 2019.

title_original: LA Artist Snuck His Own Drawing onto the Met’s Walls and Filmed It
editorial_title_zh: 洛杉矶艺术家将自己的画作偷偷挂上大都会艺术博物馆展墙并拍下视频
editorial_excerpt_zh: 大卫（萨巴斯蒂安）·米克拉茨基（David (Sabastian) Miklatski）将自己的恶作剧记录下来，公之于众。

article_text:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art became an unwitting new home for a work by the Los Angeles–based artist David (Sabastian) Miklatski, who snuck a drawing onto one of the institution’s walls and documented its time there for all the world to see.

As reported by Hyperallergic , “In a viral Instagram reel, multi-hyphenate artist David (Sabastian) Miklatski detailed the steps of creating and surreptitiously installing a drawing on one of The Met’s gallery walls last Sunday, October 25. The work in question, The MET 2027 , is an oil pastel painting depicting a Met Gala attendee ascending the staircase flanked by shrubs and photojournalists as police in riot gear beat down protestors in a fiery scene in the foreground.”

Miklatski’s Instagram reel , set to the soundtrack of The Who’s “Baba O’Riley” (aka “Teenage Wasteland”), shows his work at the Met interspersed with starry images from the Met Gala—which the artist describes as “an event where billionaires donate millions of dollars so celebrities can play dress up in the name of art”—and horrific images from Congo, Paris, Milan, Gaza, Haiti, Ukraine, and the United States.

Of the work, Miklatski says he “did it in crayon to make it extra ridiculous,” before detailing how he pulled off the caper with the aid of a baby stroller, a portable speaker loaded with sex noises, and a deceptive friend in on the ruse.
excerpt_original: David (Sabastian) Miklatski documented his caper for all the world to see.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 由马蒂斯·兰德韦尔领衔主演的武术剧情片《Lion Fist》已售出韩国、拉丁美洲及独联体版权。销售公司 Cappu Films 在东京国际电影节的 TIFFCOM 市场上透露，同由兰德韦尔主演的另一部影片《The Last Kumite》也已落户韩国……

article_text:
Mathis Landwehr -led martial arts feature “Lion Fist” has been picked up for South Korea, Latin America and the CIS.

Fellow Landwehr starrer “The Last Kumite” has also found a South Korean home, sales outfit Cappu Films revealed at the Tokyo International Film Festival ‘s TIFFCOM market.

Studio DHL has taken South Korean rights to both films. Great Movies picked up “Lion Fist” for Latin America, and Kinologistika LLC bought the title for the CIS.

Related Stories

Asif Kapadia on Bringing the ‘Profound’ ‘7 Up’ Documentary Series to a Close After More Than 60 Years: 'It's a Dream Job'

Documentary Festival IDFA to Open With 'White Tiger Column,' Following Rookie Resistance Fighters in Myanmar

Taim M. Adams directed “Lion Fist,” which casts Landwehr as Joe, a fighter who walks out of prison and learns his son needs surgery to survive. To pay for it, Joe signs up for a vicious martial arts competition carrying a $100,000 purse. Gary Daniels, Kurt McKinney, Keith Cooke and Brice Akuesson round out the cast.

Sean David Lowe and Keith W. Strandberg wrote the screenplay, and Mike Möller choreographed the fights. Lowe produced the film with Wayne Graves, and the pair hold the same credit on “The Last Kumite.”

“These deals give the films a wider international audience, and we look forward to meeting buyers for the remaining territories in Tokyo,” said Janice Woo of Cappu Films.

Ross W. Clarkson directed “The Last Kumite,” in which a fighter is forced into a lethal tournament to save his abducted daughter. Landwehr again tops the cast, joined by Cynthia Rothrock, Billy Blanks, Matthias Hues and McKinney.

“Both movies bring a nostalgic style of martial arts movies back to the screen. Already selling to many countries in the world, we trust in Cappu Films to find the right partners for new territories,” said Lowe.

Beyond the two fight films, Cappu Films is handling French action title “Red Bird,” Carter Ward’s “Step Back,” “Doors Closing” and Francesco Lucente’s fantasy “Starbright.” The company’s library spans action, horror, fantasy and arthouse fare, along with Hong Kong Golden Era titles and TV series.

年里，我花了很多时间试图寻找理由再次与他合作。如果我写了带有理查德能演的角色的剧本，我就会递给他。有时我写这个角色可能只是因为我想找个借口听他讲故事。最终我们也在其他几个项目中一起演过戏，这些年来我们成了朋友。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "毫无疑问，他也是我共事过的最好的演员之一。我知道这听起来像是人在去世时才会说的那种客套话，但我说的是真心话。理查德好得惊人。他只需要决定不把一句台词演得好笑，就能让它变得好笑。他能在几乎不怎么费力的情况下抢走整场戏的彩头。而且每隔一段时间，他就会提醒你，在那张熟悉的面孔和美妙的胡须底下，藏着一位绝大多数人无缘得见的戏路极宽的演员。", "translated": true}, {"type": 多个影视署名字数，在你不了解这个人之前，这是一个几乎荒谬的数字。比起别的什么，他是真的热爱片场。学生短片、微型独立电影、好莱坞大片、电视网情景喜剧。老实说，我并不觉得他在乎这其中有多大区别。如果他能待在片场而不是他的演员房车里，那你准能在片场找到他。只要你和他合作过一次，你就拥有了一个朋友。一年后邀请他去看一场试映、某个随机的即兴喜剧秀或者后院烧烤，只要他有空，他就会出现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "几年前，我们在达拉斯拍摄一部名为《Tonic》的电影。一天晚上喝着啤酒时，理查德告诉我，当得知自己被邀请在剧集《巴瑞》（Barry）中与老“办公空间”搭档斯蒂芬·鲁特（Stephen article_text:
The first time I met Richard Riehle , I was making one of the first things I’d ever made. It was a Funny or Die video, and my friend Tanner Thomason and I were trying to figure out how to get an actual actor to be in it. Someone suggested Richard. “Just offer it to him. I bet he’ll be down.” So we wrote him a nice letter, offered him the enormous sum of $250, and a week later we were working with a legend.

I remember arriving on set that morning and finding Richard already there, sitting by himself, reading the newspaper and drinking a root beer. He’d beaten the crew there. He didn’t need anything, didn’t seem particularly concerned that he was an actor with hundreds of credits doing a little internet video for two guys who had never really made anything before. He was just happy to be there.

Related Stories

'Coven Academy' Renewed for Season 2 at Disney

That was about 13 years ago. I spent a lot of the next 13 years trying to find reasons to work with him again. If I wrote something with a part Richard could play, I offered it to him. Sometimes I probably wrote the part because I wanted an excuse to hear his stories. We ended up acting in several other projects together, too, and over the years we became friends.

He was also, without question, one of the best actors I’ve ever worked with. I know that might sound like the sort of thing people say when someone dies, but I mean it. Richard was astonishingly good. He could make a line funny just by deciding not to make it funny. He could steal a scene without seeming to do much of anything. And every once in a while he’d remind you that underneath the familiar face and the wonderful mustache was an actor with a range most people never got to see.

Years ago, we were doing a table read for a movie called “Fear, Inc.” We’d cast Richard as the funny neighbor. The actor who was supposed to read the villain couldn’t make it that night, so Richard offered to fill in. No big deal. Just reading a few extra lines. Then he started doing the role, which he had literally worked on at home. He knew the lines of a role he wasn’t even going to play for the table read. The sweet, funny neighbor we’d all been laughing at was suddenly terrifying. I remember looking around the room and seeing jaws drop. People were genuinely stunned. It was like we’d all forgotten, for a moment, who we were sitting across from.

Richard had more than 400 acting credits, which is an almost ridiculous number until you understand the man. More than anything, he just loved being on set. Student films, tiny independent movies, major blockbusters, network sitcoms. I honestly don’t think he cared all that much about the difference. If he could hang out on set instead of in his trailer, that’s where you’d find him. And if you worked with him once, you had a friend. Invite him to a screening a year later, some random improv show, or a backyard barbecue, and if he was free, he’d show up.

A couple of years ago, we were in Dallas shooting a movie called Tonic. One night over beers, Richard told me how excited he was to have been asked to reunite with his old “Office Space” pal, Stephen Root, on an episode of “Barry.” We got to talking about his career, and he said something I’ve thought about a lot since. Richard suspected that taking so many small independent projects over the years had probably hurt his chances of getting certain television or studio jobs. Maybe people saw the sheer volume of credits and made assumptions. Maybe he’d have been better off being more selective. But he wasn’t going to change anything.

He wanted to act. As much as he could, for as long as he could. If saying yes to some tiny movie meant missing out on a bigger one, well, that was fine with him. He’d rather spend his Tuesday on a set somewhere, even a tiny set, than sit around waiting for a more prestigious phone call. I loved that about him. I think a lot of us could learn something from it.

Richard lived in the same Los Feliz spot for years. He liked being able to walk around Hillhurst and Vermont, to get out and be part of the neighborhood. He drove a Honda Civic that was something like 25 years old. Why get a new car? This one worked. It got him to set and back. That was Richard.

And he had that mustache. I’m actually wearing a mustache today partially because of Richard Riehle. Six years ago, I grew one for a movie we made together called “Faith Based.” I wasn’t sure I was going to keep it. Richard told me I should. He said growing his own mustache was one of the best decisions he’d ever made. It fit his face, he explained, and gave him something distinctive. Coming from a man whose mustache belongs in the same conversation as Sam Elliott’s and Burt Reynolds’, I took that advice pretty seriously. I haven’t shaved it since. I suppose that’s a pretty small thing to carry forward from a friendship, but I like knowing that a little piece of Richard will be looking back at me in the mirror every morning.

When I think about Richard now, I don’t really think about his filmography, impressive as it is. I think about that first morning. The newspaper and the root beer. A man who’d already been in more movies than I could count, sitting patiently on the set of a $250 internet video in Canoga Park, ready to give it everything he had for a comedy sketch.

He gave that little project just as much as he would have given a studio movie. I don’t think it ever occurred to him to do otherwise. Richard just loved being an actor.

Luke Barnett is an actor, writer, and filmmaker whose credits include AMC’s “Dark Winds,” Apple TV+’s “For All Mankind” and Peacock’s “The Burbs.” His recent filmmaking work includes the viral short “The Crossing Over Express,” currently being developed as a feature, and the Fangoria-produced “Goodbye, Monster,” which just premiered at Fantastic Fest. He has also worked on nearly a dozen projects with the late Richard Riehle, though not nearly enough.
